findings.title: Open agent enrollment: RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET not set anywhere
findings.evidence: enrollment_secret = os.getenv("RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET") or ...; compose.yaml and k8s set no value, so POST /api/v1/agents mints a bearer token for anyone who can reach :8010 (published on 0.0.0.0). Known since recon (Step 0).
findings.recommendation: Set RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET from an untracked .env/Secret in compose and k8s; fail closed (refuse to start or refuse registration) when unset outside dev.
findings.disposition_rationale: Require RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET from an untracked .env, and bind the app port to 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: Plaintext DB credentials in tracked files (compose.yaml, k8s/secret.yaml, ci.yml)
findings.evidence: POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <dev-default> (compose.yaml:6, :28 URL; k8s/secret.yaml:8, :13; .github/workflows/ci.yml:34, :52). Default dev value, public in git history; Postgres is not published to the host in compose.
findings.recommendation: Move to an untracked .env / k8s Secret created out of band; use a random password; keep CI's throwaway DB but bind it to 127.0.0.1.
findings.disposition_rationale: The dev-only default, and Postgres isn't published. Changing the password on an existing volume needs ALTER USER; not worth the risk before the deadline.

findings.title: Public interactive API docs: /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json
findings.evidence: app = FastAPI(title="Agent Relay", version="0.1.0", lifespan=lifespan) leaves docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url at defaults. Verified 2026-09-27: all three return 200 without auth on a scratch instance.
findings.recommendation: Pass docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None in non-dev environments (or gate them behind auth).
findings.disposition_rationale: Info disclosure only, and localhost-bound after the K-001 fix.

findings.title: Postgres 'DETAIL: Failing row contains (...)' can echo task payloads into logs and span events
findings.evidence: hide_parameters=True (database.py:141) removes SQLAlchemy's [parameters], but psycopg exceptions include the server's DETAIL line with the failing row's values; logging_config.py:43 writes formatException(), and OTel records exception messages on spans. Credentials cannot appear (tokens stored as SHA-256), but task input/output can. Found in Step 2.
findings.recommendation: Scrub exception messages for psycopg IntegrityError/DETAIL before logging/recording (log exception type + constraint name only), or set Postgres log verbosity for client errors to TERSE on the connection.

findings.title: Race (Postgres): lease recovery can requeue a task that already has a newer live attempt
findings.evidence: recover_expired_in_session reads expired attempts, then db.get(Task) and checks task.status == 'processing' without a row lock; under READ COMMITTED a concurrent claim may have started attempt N+1, and recovery flips the task back to 'queued' -> duplicate processing. From Step 1 code reading, not reproduced.
findings.recommendation: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the task (and attempt) rows in recovery, or a guarded UPDATE ... WHERE status='processing' AND attempt_count = <expected>.
findings.disposition_rationale: Postgres races, from code reading; integrity rather than confidentiality.

findings.title: Race (Postgres): recovery vs heartbeat / terminal submission (lost updates)
findings.evidence: heartbeat (storage.py:215) and commit_terminal (storage.py:236-249) read the attempt and check the lease without a row lock; a concurrent recovery commit can be overwritten (an expired attempt gets its lease extended, or an expired/requeued task is marked completed). Narrow window. From Step 1 code reading.
findings.recommendation: Lock the attempt/task rows (FOR UPDATE) in heartbeat and commit_terminal, or make the writes conditional on outcome='processing'.
findings.disposition_rationale: Postgres races, from code reading; integrity rather than confidentiality.

findings.title: Race (Postgres): concurrent creates with the same Idempotency-Key return 500 instead of the existing task
findings.evidence: create_task checks for an existing (sender_id, idempotency_key) row, then inserts (storage.py:138); two concurrent requests both pass the check and the loser hits uq_task_sender_idempotency -> unhandled IntegrityError -> 500 (main.py retry loop only handles 'locked'). From Step 1 code reading.
findings.recommendation: Catch IntegrityError on uq_task_sender_idempotency and re-read the existing row (or use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING).
findings.disposition_rationale: Postgres races, from code reading; integrity rather than confidentiality.

findings.title: User-level Claude setting (advisorModel) leaked a server-side 'advisor' tool into headless runs
findings.evidence: Found by the Step 4 canary/probe: ~/.claude/settings.json advisorModel added an 'advisor' tool to every headless responder run. Neutralised with --settings '{"advisorModel":""}'. Other user/project settings are still loaded by default (see capability-table A9).
findings.recommendation: Add --setting-sources "" (or --safe-mode) to the responder and model-review invocations so only explicit --settings apply; keep the canary as a regression check after CLI upgrades.
findings.disposition_rationale: Add --setting-sources "" to the responder and the model review, then re-run the canary.

findings.title: verify-recovery.sh does not check that the backlog drained
findings.evidence: Checks are ready, version, a fresh 60 s probe, 5xx rate 0, alert cleared. In Step 5 it passed while 746 tasks were stranded in the queue; relay_queue_depth / relay_queue_oldest_age_seconds are not checked.
findings.recommendation: Add a check that relay_queue_depth returns to its pre-incident level (or oldest queued age < N s) within the wait window; report stranded work explicitly.

findings.title: L1 rollback during a non-deploy outage passes every precondition; human approval is the only gate
findings.evidence: Computed in Step 4 from the drill's recorded facts: with a DB outage, an L1 rollback to previous_version would reach require_approval (all 6 preconditions pass: alert firing, target == previous_version, image exists, deployed < 24h, no recent rollback, under limit). Nothing checks that the failure correlates with the deploy.
findings.recommendation: Add a precondition tying rollback to the change: e.g. the failing series' 5xx ratio was ~0 on previous_version and rose after running_deployed_at, or require a second approver / explicit confirmation text when the failure started long after the deploy.
findings.disposition_rationale: By design for an L1 action, where human approval is the gate. Mandatory precondition if rollback is ever promoted to L2: a deploy-correlation check (the failing version was deployed shortly before activeAt, and the previous version was healthy).

findings.title: Evidence secret scan misses KEY: value secrets; committed incident evidence contains the dev DB password
findings.evidence: Also reported by the model (M-004) and verified: incident-response/incidents/INC-20260926-183037-.../evidence/changed-files/compose.yaml:6 contains 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <dev-default>' although the manifest says secret_scan passed. The value is the public dev default, so nothing new is exposed, but the scan would miss a real secret in the same shape.
findings.recommendation: Extend redact() and the scan to *_PASSWORD/*_SECRET/*_TOKEN key=value and YAML forms, and scan for the actual RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET/POSTGRES_PASSWORD values like the Grafana password.
findings.disposition_rationale: Redact key-like secret values at evidence-collection time and extend the scan. Do NOT edit already-committed incident evidence (it would break its manifest hashes; the value is the public dev default).
